findings.explanation: The new RuleSnoozeEndpoint.post() fetches a Rule or AlertRule solely by the URL-supplied rule_id (Rule.objects.get(id=rule_id) / AlertRule.objects.get(id=rule_id)) without filtering by the project (or organization) passed to the handler. Although the route includes organization_slug/project_slug and the base permission ProjectAlertRulePermission grants POST via 'project:write'/'project:admin'/'alerts:write' (project.py:77-83), the object-level check can_edit_alert_rule() is the only thing binding the user to the specific rule. For a 'Rule' whose owner is None (or a rule owned by a team the user is not on), the check falls through to 'return True' after failing the team check, but more critically, for any AlertRule (metric rule) the 'rule.owner' lookup will not resolve to the project, so any user with project:write in the URL project can snooze an AlertRule from a different project/organization that they have no access to. The endpoint never verifies that the fetched rule belongs to the project in the request, allowing cross-tenant snoozing.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the object fetch to the project in the request, e.g. Rule.objects.get(id=rule_id, project_id=project.id) and AlertRule.objects.get(id=rule_id, organization_id=project.organization.id), or add an explicit ownership check in can_edit_alert_rule() that verifies the rule's project/organization matches the request's project (rule.project_id == project.id for Rule; rule.organization_id == project.organization.id for AlertRule) before allowing the operation.
